summary: Remote receipts, acks, prompt bindings and Git/quota intents move from project-workspace.json into a sibling remote-state.json. The project checkpoint keeps only schema_version, workspace, sessions, subtabs and the workspace revision (now workspace_revision, owned by the pool), so a build without remote state reads it unchanged. Both files are replaced under the one project-workspace.lock: every CAS baseline is checked, all replacements are fsynced, then core is renamed before remote, so a crash between renames leaves a remote reservation unresolved (unknown outcome) rather than a remote success the workspace does not show. A pre-split checkpoint with inline remote_workspace is migrated on restore (remote-state.json written first, then the inline copy dropped).

notes: The remote feature does not exist yet (ZE-520), so the validator 'a checkpoint written with --features remote loads in the default build' is proven structurally here (the core file carries no remote keys) and end-to-end in ZE-520. Tests that edited the inline remote_workspace now read a combined view (tests/remote_workspace.rs saved_state) and write it back as a legacy checkpoint, which also exercises the migration path. A missing project-workspace.json resets remote-state.json, as deleting the single file did before. Remaining crash window: between the two fsynced renames a combined commit can leave the workspace advanced with its receipt still null; that receipt reports unknown_outcome and quota/worktree reconcile refuses it as stale (no false success, no replay). No new unwrap/expect/panic in non-test code, no unsafe beyond the existing flock calls moved unchanged.
